headline: A McDonald's customer has sued the chain in a proposed nationwide class action, claiming its AI pricing system helped coordinate menu prices across franchise restaurants.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a nationwide antitrust suit over AI-assisted pricing at a chain with nearly 14,000 US restaurants, first reported on 5 Oct, though the claims are allegations that McDonald's denies.
importance_line: Diners are alleged to be paying prices coordinated through a shared AI system, and the case could test how antitrust law treats AI pricing at franchise chains, but the claims are unproven and McDonald's denies them.
summary: Reuters reports that an Illinois customer filed a proposed class action (a lawsuit on behalf of many people) in Chicago federal court on 2 Oct 2026, alleging that McDonald's breaks US antitrust law by coordinating menu prices with its franchisees through an AI-powered system trained on non-public data. The suit cites Reuters' investigation of 29 Sep 2026, which our 5 Oct edition carried, into how McDonald's AI recommends prices at nearly 14,000 US restaurants, and McDonald's said on 5 Oct that the allegations are speculative and uninformed and that franchisees set their own prices.
notes: Read as the Reuters wire text on The Economic Times because the Reuters page returns 401; cross-checked with PYMNTS, National Technology News, Livemint and Law Commentary. The filing (2 Oct) precedes the window but it was first reported and answered by McDonald's on 5 Oct, so the pool score is kept. Follow-up of the Reuters investigation of 29 Sep that our 5 Oct edition carried (entry 112, via Futurism).
